transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

It is quite common for plastics to stay wet and for glasses to have drips on a Bosch Serie 4, as these machines often rely on condensation drying rather than a heated element, meaning water can bead up on cool plastic surfaces. However, if your china and glassware are also coming out soaking wet or cold, it suggests the machine might not be reaching the high temperatures needed for proper evaporation or that the rinse aid level is low. The most likely cause here is simply insufficient rinse aid, which helps water sheet off dishes rather than sitting in droplets. To check this safely, please switch off and unplug the dishwasher, then locate the rinse aid dispenser usually near the door frame and top it up if it looks empty or low.
Ok, the rinse aid symbol is actually lit on the display, and it is empty. I use all-in-one tablets though, does it still need topping up?

Yes, you still need to top up the rinse aid even when using all-in-one tablets because those tablets rarely contain enough rinse aid for optimal drying performance. The lit symbol suggests it is empty, so please switch off and unplug the dishwasher before refilling the dispenser with liquid rinse aid. This will help water sheet off your dishes rather than sitting in droplets. Once you have done that, run a standard cycle to see if the wetness improves.
Ok, I'll top it up with rinse aid. Anything else I should change, like settings? I've been using Eco 50 every time.

Yes, the Eco 50 programme often results in wetter dishes because it uses lower water temperatures and skips the heated drying phase to save energy. I recommend switching to a standard or intensive programme for your next load to see if that improves the drying. You should also ensure you are not opening the door immediately after the cycle finishes, as this lets steam escape before the condensation process is complete. Please try one of these programmes and let me know how the results compare.
